hypotheses.text: The reflow oven profile was incorrectly re-tuned after the Zone 7 heater element replacement, leading to excessive solder fluidity and bridging.
The solder paste used for the affected lot was older than optimal, leading to reduced viscosity and slumping, resulting in solder bridges.
The squeegee pressure during solder paste printing was not optimal, leading to either smearing or poor paste definition, which caused solder bridges.
High room humidity negatively impacted the solder paste's rheology, causing it to slump and form solder bridges.
The specific operator running the line for the affected lot may have contributed to process variations leading to solder bridges.

D1.text: A cross-functional team has been assembled to address complaint C-2026-031 regarding solder bridging on product ECU-PCB-7, lot L2611.

D2.text: Complaint C-2026-031 reported solder bridging on product ECU-PCB-7, lot L2611 [complaint C-2026-031]. A total of 14 units out of 500 shipped units were affected [complaint C-2026-031]. The defect is characterized as a continuous blob of solder connecting the top two pins of the three-pin header on the left side of the board [Defect: solder_bridge].

D3.text: All potentially affected lots have been placed on hold. These include lots L2609, L2610, L2611, L2612, L2613, and L2614 [hold_lots].

D4.text: The root cause is that the reflow profile was left unverified after the Zone 7 heater element replacement (WO-388) and drifted out of control, leading to an increase in reflow peak temperature across a window of lots [Chart: reflow peak temp by lot]. Most lots produced in the affected window, specifically 5 out of 6 lots (L2609, L2610, L2612, L2613, L2614), exceeded the peak temperature limit of 250.0 °C [peak_limit_breaches]. The complained-about lot L2611 had a reflow peak temperature of 248.7 °C [Lot record L2611] and a time above liquidus of 83.0 s [Lot record L2611]. This root cause was verified by a Welch t-test comparing 6 defect lots to 27 good lots, which showed a statistically significant effect of +7.6 °C mean reflow peak temperature (p-value 0.000221) [Welch t-test]. The issue escaped detection because the reflow profile verification, required after oven maintenance, was pending for WO-388 [Control plan item 6].

D5.text: Implement a mandatory reflow profile verification procedure to be performed immediately after any reflow oven maintenance, specifically after heater element replacements or re-tuning events. This procedure will require a golden board profiler run to confirm peak temperature is within 235-250 °C and time above liquidus is within 45-90 s [Control plan item 6].

D6.text: Effectiveness of the permanent corrective action will be verified by monitoring reflow profile data for all production lots for a period of 3 months following any oven maintenance event. All profile data will be reviewed weekly to ensure adherence to the specified peak temperature and time above liquidus limits [Control plan item 6]. Any deviation will trigger an immediate line stop and re-profiling.

D7.text: To prevent recurrence, the PFMEA will be updated in row 14 [PFMEA row 14] to strengthen the prevention control for 'Profile verification after any oven maintenance'. The Control Plan will be updated in item 6 [Control plan item 6] to explicitly state the requirement for immediate profile verification after any oven maintenance, including specific sign-off procedures.

D8.text: The team is commended for their swift action and thorough investigation in identifying the root cause and implementing corrective actions. Their dedication ensures continuous improvement in our manufacturing processes.
